title: Session Surface Cuebook — personal PRD jot
content:
Context / intent:
Quick personal jot for an incremental feature: lightweight session surface for client apps that need a small in-memory UX layer to surface partial responses, cues, and fallback affordances while a long-running generation or multimodal asset fetch completes. Not a formal PRD yet — just organizing user stories, constraints, and rough rollout ideas before I sync with design and infra.

Why:
- Customers embed assistant-like features but want better perceived latency and clear fallback affordances when the full response is delayed or truncated (mobile networks, heavy generation, backend tool calls).
- Redwood serving runtimes give streaming tokens, KV cache, and partial KV snapshots — we can expose a tiny surface to clients that’s cheap and compatible with hosted/dedicated/private deployments.

Primary hypothesis:
If we provide a minimal standardized session surface (API + UX primitives) that surfaces partial answers, confidence cues, and graceful fallbacks, product teams will ship smoother experiences with fewer custom engineering changes and lower token waste.

Target user personas:
- Mobile product engineer: wants perceived latency improvements without changing server-side model policies.
- Customer success/engineering: wants predictable behaviors for timeouts and tool call failures.
- UX designer: wants standardized cues (loading, partial answer, degraded mode) to avoid reinventing microcopy.

High-level feature sketch:
- API: session-surface.create(session_id, options) -> returns a handle.
- session-surface.patch(stream_chunk) -> optional metadata: {confidence_est, complete: bool, sources: [strings], partial_summary}.
- client-side SDKs render three states: partial-answer (first chunk with content), progress-cue (spinner + ETA if available), degraded-mode (short summary + CTA: retry, expand, or switch-model).
- explicit signal for tool-bound waits: server tells client "awaiting-tool" so UI can render stepper.

User stories (rough):
1) Mobile engineer: "As an app developer, I want a small preview of the assistant's first paragraph ASAP so users can begin to read while the rest is generated."
  - Acceptance: Preview shows within 300ms of first token, consistent across hosted/dedicated.
2) Product manager: "As PM, I want the UI to show a clear fallback when a call exceeds 6s so users don't think the app crashed."
  - Acceptance: Fallback mode presented, with CTA to retry or request condensed version; backend logs mark event.
3) SRE: "As SRE, I want the surface to be cheap to store and expire after 1 minute by default to avoid long-lived sessions."
  - Acceptance: Default TTL enforced; metrics exposed for TTL expirations.

Important constraints / non-goals:
- Non-goal: full conversation state sync or session store replacement. This is a lightweight transient UX surface (short TTL).
- Must work with private deployments (no external callbacks). Use control-plane-free signals (embed metadata in streaming chunks or event stream).
- Keep additional token cost minimal; provide opt-in summarization/shallow caching features.

Metrics / success signals:
- Adoption: percent of trial accounts enabling session surface within 30 days of SDK release.
- UX: reduction in abandonment rate for flows with long generation (>3s) by 15%.
- Cost: no more than 5% increase in tokens served net after enabling previews (measured across pilot customers).
- Reliability telemetry: fallback events per 1000 requests, average time-to-first-chunk.

API sketch (informal):
- POST /v1/sessionsurface {session_id, model_hint, ttl, partial_policy: [first_token|first_sentence|summary]} returns surface_id
- Server emits stream events: {type: "chunk", text: "...", partial_summary?: "...", confidence?: 0.9, state: "awaiting-tool"|"complete"|"partial"}
- Client can request condensed fallback: POST /v1/sessionsurface/{surface_id}/condense?budget=64 -> returns short summary (cheaper model)

Client UX primitives (quick list):
- partial-snippet: show first N chars; highlights source tokens that are solid (confidence > 0.8).
- progress-cue: spinner + optional ETA when server provides progress hints.
- degraded-card: 1–2 sentence summary + actions (retry, request-brief, open-full-thread).

Rollout plan (sketch):
- Phase 0: internal dogfood. Integrate with console chat sample app and one Redwood-hosted dashboard flow.
- Phase 1: SDK beta for 5 customers (mix of mobile + web), default OFF, opt-in via header. Collect metrics.
- Phase 2: public SDK, examples, console toggle, and a few prebuilt microcopy templates.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to surface ETA reliably? Only some model runtimes can estimate remaining tokens/time. Fall back to heuristic (token-rate average) when not available.
- Security: ensure no leakage of partial results across sessions in Dedicated/Private. Need strong surface_id entropy and per-tenant namespaces.
- Cost model: should preview consumption be billed differently? Likely billed as usual tokens, but consider a lowered-metered mode for condensed fallbacks.
- SDK compatibility: do we add to existing JS/Swift SDKs or ship as a tiny separate package?

Short TODOs (my next actions):
- Draft a compact proto for event stream with infra (Mika) by next Thu.
- Prototype client rendering in mobile sample app (Ethan) — get a before/after abandonment metric.
- Write short Confluence spec and add to linked artifacts.
- Decide on TTL defaults (1m/5m/ephemeral) and add to SRE checklist.

Notes / references:
- Related idea: 'prefetch priming profiles' (see linked doc) — could reduce time-to-first-chunk for common prompts.
- Slack thread: #ux-assistant-latency (search: "session surface") has early design sketches.

Rough copy ideas for degraded mode microcopy (UX):
- "Sorry for the delay — here's a quick summary while I finish the rest. Tap to expand."
- Buttons: "Get short version", "Retry now", "Open full response"

Hand-wavey implementation thoughts:
- Use streaming metadata hooks in the runtimes to attach partial_summary and confidence. If not available, server-side cheap summarizer (small model) can create a 1–2 sentence snippet after receiving first N tokens.
- Provide a pluggable fallback policy that can switch to quantized or cheaper model for condense API call.

If this resonates, next sync: 30m with Mika + Ethan to align infra and UX feasibility. Bring a short prototype (JS + mobile snippet) to demo.

End of jot.
